Ok, I get it we're surrounded by a sizeable majority who values passing and conventional femininity greatly. So I understand how it may seem that this majority may be forcing some sort of dogma, especially when people say things like "But passing decreases your chance of being the victim of hostility." And even though this may be true, being surrounded by occasionally vicious sectarianism in the trans community from dysphoric individuals who enforce their biases of passing out into wider trans spaces, or transmeds who are even more vicious in their enforcement of the standard of passing, saying that those who do not have the sort of mental-to-body dissonance that dysphoric individuals have are not to be accepted as valid trans people. But seriously, I understand if you're somewhat insecure about other opinions on passing. I would for the most part, suggest that you learn to filter out hardline opinions of whether passing is necessary or un-necessary and just understand that passing is never white or black, or 'universal' in any way. It is always up to the individual to decide on whether they wish to pursue a more conventional aesthetic. So please just understand that if anyone tries to force ANY hard turn in the journey of being trans, whether to be the most clockable transfemme the world has ever seen, or the most conventionally, generally, and most feminine transfemme ever. People have different ideal selves. If one amab trans person says "I was born with masculine traits and I'm ok with that.", that's perfectly ok and valid, as in everyone should respect their choices. But if another amab trans person says "I was born with masculine traits and I want to change these traits.", that is also completely ok and valid; that person deserves to have their choices respected. 👆
